text:
Druck on why the best risk mgmt system is a combo of gut feel and "P&L watching"

sounds crude & silly prima facie, but is both widespread in practice in L/S + effective (given prerequisite 20-30 yrs of watching tape to develop instinct)

"vaguely right > precisely wrong"

quotedTweet.text:
really good commentary on risk mgmt

(gut feel + P&L watching) > quantitative VAR/beta model

DRUCKENMILLER:

-"But the reason I love the human side as opposed to the quantitative side is there's nothing like my P&L."

-"My risk management system has always been what I've described, that knowledge, and then my gut, and watching my daily P&L....instead of going to some quantitative VAR or beta model, to go, “Oh, I'm okay, the model says I'm okay.”

-"To me, these models are not only okay, they can get you in huge trouble by causing you a false sense of security when things start going awry."

-"If you are an intuitive human trader, you should be able to use your instinct to just start cutting when things aren't acting right." (2009 intvw)

***

from article "risk mgmt pt 3: USA (Use Stops Always)":

"The truth is that after you’ve traded markets long enough, the combo of watching the P&L - 'what's getting worse?' - paired with gut feel is often your best defense against drawdowns, better than anything else in your toolkit, and if you ask any veteran trader they will probably co-sign this."

best PM/risk mgr I've ever seen operated that way -- druck put it into words perfectly though

flies against academia/theory...(gut feel + P&L watching) > all other risk mgmt systems
